--- title: "[Graph.katz_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get Katz centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L42616-L42839){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.katz_centrality( alpha=0.1, beta=1.0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, normalized=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Katz centrality](/assets/graphs/katz-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node directed graph shaded by Katz centrality with alpha 0.5, which counts incoming walks. D receives walks from A, B and C and scores 0.32, E, fed through D, 0.26, B and C 0.16, and the source A, which nothing reaches, 0.11." width="100%"} Katz centrality measures node influence based on the number of walks of all lengths reaching the node, with walks weighted by `α^length`: `x = α · Aᵀ · x + β` where α is the attenuation factor, `Aᵀ` is the transpose of the adjacency matrix, and `β` is a bias vector: by default the same baseline for every node, but `beta=` can also give each node its own. For directed graphs, this counts incoming paths, making it suitable for measuring "prestige" or "influence received". Key differences from other centralities: - PageRank: uses teleportation and out-degree normalization - Eigenvector: only considers infinite-length walks (principal eigenvector) - Alpha centrality: uses `A` instead of `Aᵀ` (outgoing vs incoming) - Katz: weights walks by path length, considers all finite walks Because every node receives the same baseline `β`, nodes that nothing points to still get a non-zero score, which makes Katz centrality well behaved on directed acyclic graphs where eigenvector centrality degenerates. Typical uses include: - ranking papers, patents, or packages by direct and indirect citations or dependencies - measuring prestige in follower or endorsement networks - scoring nodes when short chains of influence should count more than long ones The scores are found by fixed-point iteration starting from `β`, then (by default) rescaled to sum to `1`. Edge weights are ignored. For undirected graphs `Aᵀ = A`, so with the default `beta=` the result is identical to `alpha_centrality()` with the same `alpha=`. If `alpha=` is at or above `1 / λ_max` the iteration diverges and a `RuntimeWarning` is emitted (the scores are then meaningless), so keep `alpha=` comfortably small. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Attenuation factor for walk lengths. Must be smaller than the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue (typically < `0.2` for safety). Higher values give more weight to longer paths. Defaults to `0.1`. For a directed acyclic graph the largest eigenvalue is `0`, so any positive value converges. [beta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | dict[int | str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Baseline score each node contributes, as a single number for all nodes (default `1.0`) or as a dictionary mapping every node (by ID or label) to its own baseline. Per-node baselines let some nodes matter more as sources of influence, for example to weight citations by the citing paper's venue. A single number only scales the raw scores, so with the default `normalized=True` every positive value gives the same result; it matters with `normalized=False`. A dictionary that leaves out a node raises a `ValueError`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations. Defaults to `100`. If the scores have not converged by then, the values from the last iteration are returned and a `RuntimeWarning` is emitted. Convergence slows as `alpha=` approaches `1 / λ_max`. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence threshold. Iteration stops once the largest absolute change of any node's (unnormalized) score between two iterations falls below `tol=`. Defaults to `1e-6`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name used to store the scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), the column is named `"katz_centrality"`. An existing column with the same name is overwritten. Only used when `return_dict=` is `False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the scores as a dictionary and leave the node DataFrame untouched. If `False` (default), store the scores under `attr_name=` and return the graph for method chaining. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), rescale the scores to sum to `1` so they can be compared across graphs. If `False`, return the raw solution of `x = α · Aᵀ · x + β`, whose scale follows `beta=` (this matches NetworkX's `normalized=False`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to Katz centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. With the default `normalized=True` the scores sum to `1.0`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Katz centrality (Katz, 1953) generalizes eigenvector centrality by giving every node a baseline contribution and geometrically discounting influence with distance. The iteration converges to the closed-form solution $c = (I - \alpha A^\top)^{-1} \beta$ (with $\beta$ the vector of baselines, $\beta \mathbf{1}$ for a single number), which exists only when $\alpha < 1/\lambda_{\max}(A)$; sensible defaults sit around $\alpha \approx 0.1$ and rarely above $0.2$. For directed graphs the transpose matters: high Katz signals prestige (many incoming paths, weighted toward short ones), while for undirected graphs $A^\top = A$ and the metric coincides with alpha centrality. Final scores are normalized to sum to $1$ by default so they can be compared across graphs of different sizes; this also means a constant $\beta$ cancels out of the result, while a per-node $\beta$ (or `normalized=False`) does not. ## Examples {.doc-examples} "D" receives incoming edges both directly from "A" and indirectly via "B" and "C", so it accumulates the highest Katz score, while "A", which nothing points to, scores lowest: ::: {#65e4ff3f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("A", "D")]) ) scores = graph.katz_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0.226, 'B': 0.249, 'C': 0.251, 'D': 0.274} ``` ::: ::: A smaller `alpha=` weights short walks much more heavily than long ones, so all scores stay close to the uniform `0.25`. A larger value lets the long walk A-B-C-D count too, and the gap between the source A and the sink D widens: ::: {#7ae0fcf0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} low = graph.katz_centrality(alpha=0.05, return_dict=True) high = graph.katz_centrality(alpha=0.5, return_dict=True) { graph.get_label_from_id(nid): (round(low[nid], 3), round(high[nid], 3)) for nid in sorted(low) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'A': (0.238, 0.151), 'B': (0.25, 0.226), 'C': (0.25, 0.264), 'D': (0.262, 0.358)} ``` ::: ::: Passing `beta=` as a dictionary gives each node its own baseline. Making "C" a stronger source of influence (baseline `5` instead of `1`) lifts "C" to the top and keeps its successor "D" high, while "A" and "B" fall back: ::: {#a7d11937 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} baselines = {"A": 1, "B": 1, "C": 5, "D": 1} scores = graph.katz_centrality(alpha=0.5, beta=baselines, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'A': 0.079, 'B': 0.119, 'C': 0.455, 'D': 0.347} ``` ::: ::: With `normalized=False` the raw fixed point is returned instead. Each score is the node's baseline plus `alpha=` times the scores of the nodes pointing at it, so "D" gets `1 + 0.5 * (1 + 1.75) = 2.375`: ::: {#e67ea23a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = graph.katz_centrality(alpha=0.5, normalized=False, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(raw.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {'A': 1.0, 'B': 1.5, 'C': 1.75, 'D': 2.375} ``` ::: ::: With `return_dict=False` (the default) the scores are stored in the node DataFrame under `attr_name=` and the graph is returned for chaining: ::: {#96ae4520 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( graph .katz_centrality(alpha=0.5, attr_name="katz") .get_node_df() .select(["label", "katz"]) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
